svg.title: Simultaneous fictitious play in Matching Pennies

cc:Work.dc:title: Simultaneous fictitious play in Matching Pennies
cc:Work.dc:description: Original numerical simulation for the Computational Game Theory course. Matching Pennies uses Alice payoff matrix [[1,-1],[-1,1]] and Bob payoff -A, as in _variables.yml games.matching_pennies. There are 5,000 rounds, beginning with (H,H). In each later round both players simultaneously best respond to the opponent empirical distribution from all earlier rounds; both break ties toward H. First ten profiles: HH, HT, HT, TT, TT, TT, TH, TH, TH, TH. Left: cumulative empirical frequencies of H for Alice and Bob. Right: exact unsmoothed saddle-point gap max_i(A y)_i - min_j(x A)_j = |2 p_A(H)-1|+|2 p_B(H)-1| after each round. Final H counts: 2,475 for each player; final frequencies: 0.495 each; final gap: 0.02. Both panels use logarithmic horizontal axes; the right panel also uses a logarithmic vertical axis. All 5,000 computed observations are plotted with no smoothing.
